walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 2: Investigating the Creative and Cultural Industries — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 2: Investigating the Creative and Cultural Industries brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 2: Investigating the Creative and Cultural Industries.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique uses crossing lines for tone?
options: Stippling
Cross-hatching
Smudging
Tracing
Lines
Dots
Circles
Squares
An Italian school of artists.
Relief is for paper, intaglio is for fabric.
Strong contrast between light and dark to model three-dimensional form.
Painting only at night.

mcqs.q: What is appropriation in postmodern art?
options: Stealing artwork to sell.
Deliberately reusing existing images or styles, often to comment on originality.
An Italian school of artists.
Painting in an old-fashioned style.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between relief and intaglio printing?
options: Relief prints from raised surfaces; intaglio prints from incised lines below the surface.
Relief is for paper, intaglio is for fabric.
Painting in an old-fashioned style.
They are different names for the same process.
